{{Quote|On Concord Dawn, cheating is a capital offense.|Hovrak|<ref name="YJK" />}}
'''Concord Dawn''' was an agricultural frontier [[Planet/Legends|world]] in the [[Mandalore sector/Legends|Mandalore sector]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. The planet had strong ties to the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorians]]; its population shared many Mandalorian values, and genetic markers specific to the natives of Concord Dawn were present throughout the Mandalorian populace. Concord Dawn was a flashpoint for the [[Mandalorian Civil War (True Mandalorians)|Mandalorian Civil War]] in [[58 BBY/Legends|58 BBY]], when the [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]] of [[Tor Vizsla]] [[Battle of Concord Dawn|scattered]] the [[True Mandalorians]] of [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|Mandalore]] [[Jaster Mereel]], a native of Concord Dawn. Mereel escaped and turned the tables on Vizsla with the help of a native [[Gender/Legends|boy]], [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]], orphaned by the Death Watch. Jango's son [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] would later settle on Concord Dawn before being exiled for the murder of his superior [[Officer/Legends|officer]].

Law on Concord Dawn, which could be strict in execution and punishment, was maintained by the [[Journeyman Protector/Legends|Journeyman Protectors]]. Among their numbers were Mereel, [[Fett (Elder Journeyman Protector)|Jango Fett's father]], Boba Fett, and [[Cort Davin]], one of the [[Cuy'val Dar]] trainers of the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]]. Other members of the law on Concord Dawn included [[Sheckil/Legends|Sheckil]], who became a [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenant]] in the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], and a [[Devaronian/Legends|Devaronian]] [[Unidentified Devaronian magistrate|senior magistrate]] who in [[24 ABY/Legends|24 ABY]] used his position to route [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Prison/Legends|prisoners]] to be executed by the anti-Human [[Diversity Alliance]]. Members of the Grand Army were even influenced by the traditions of Concord Dawn's Protectors, such as [[Sergeant/Legends|Sergeant]] [[Fox (501st Legion)/Legends|Fox]], who intended to retire to become a Protector at the end of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].

==Description==
{{Quote|...Concord Dawn, an agricultural world in the Mandalore sector.|[[Cradossk/Legends|Cradossk]]|<ref name="The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett">''[[The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett]]''</ref>}}
[[File:ConcordDawn-JFOS.jpg|thumb|right|200px|A city on Concord Dawn.]]
Concord Dawn was an [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] in the [[Mandalore sector/Legends|Mandalore sector]],<ref name="EAOC" /> located near the border between the Outer and [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]].<ref name="TEA" /> Like the rest of its [[Sector/Legends|sector]], it was frontier country, covered in jungles, forests, deserts and plains.<ref name="APM" /> The planet was principally an agricultural world, backwards in development, and its plains were tilled by the planet's [[Farm/Legends|farmers]] to meager effect.<ref name="APM" /><ref name="FF">{{FactFile|124|VIZ 1-4|Vizsla}}</ref> The region of Concord Dawn around the [[Clan Fett|Fett family]] [[Fett homestead|homestead]] and its nearby [[City/Legends|village]] was arid and dusty, though still capable of growing crops.<ref name="OS" />

==History==
===Mandalorian conflicts===
[[File:Concorddawn.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Jaster Mereel rescues Jango Fett on Concord Dawn.]]
Concord Dawn was conquered by the [[Mandalorian Crusaders|Mandalorians]] during their crusades thousands of years before the [[Mandalorian Civil War (True Mandalorians)|Mandalorian Civil War]].<ref name="TEA" />
Before becoming [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|Mandalore]], [[Jaster Mereel]] was a native of Concord Dawn and a [[Journeyman Protector/Legends|Journeyman Protector]] on that world. Mereel, a man of strict moral codes, killed a superior [[Officer/Legends|officer]] for the man's corruption and was [[Exile (punishment)/Legends|exiled]] as a result. While Mereel eventually rose to be leader of the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorians]],<ref name="HOTM">{{InsiderCite|80|The History of the Mandalorians: Exploring the Evolution of a Mighty Race of Warriors}}</ref> his position on Concord Dawn was taken up by a man named [[Fett (Elder Journeyman Protector)|Fett]].<ref name="OS" />

Over half a century before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], the [[Mandalorian Civil War (True Mandalorians)|Mandalorian Civil War]] broke out when the [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]], a splinter group of [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorians]] led by [[Tor Vizsla]], launched a coup against Mereel's [[True Mandalorians]]. In [[58 BBY/Legends|58 BBY]], the war came to Concord Dawn. The Death Watch [[Battle of Concord Dawn|triumphed over]] Mereel's men, and the True Mandalorians were forced to scatter into hiding as Vizsla hunted them down. Mereel fled to the safety of Fett's farm, where his replacement kept the Mandalore and his men fed and hidden. Vizsla and the Death Watch tracked them down anyway, and they took Fett's son [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango]] hostage as they beat Fett for information on Mereel. An attempt by Fett's [[Jango Fett's mother|wife]] gave Jango an opportunity to escape&mdash;and run directly into Mereel&mdash;but Vizsla's men [[Death/Legends|killed]] the elder Fetts, took their daughter [[Arla Fett|Arla]] captive, and burned down their fields to kill Mereel. Jango helped the True Mandalorians escape Mereel's trap, and Mereel took Jango with him to go after Vizsla. After leaving the Fett farm, Vizsla moved to the nearest [[City/Legends|village]], intending to pillage it for two days before moving on to the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] of [[Moonus Mandel/Legends|Moonus Mandel]]. Mereel and his men caught the Death Watch in ambush there, wiping out many of them, though Vizsla escaped. After securing the town, the True Mandalorians pulled off Concord Dawn.<ref name="OS" />

===Later events===
The [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] came to Concord Dawn in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]] in search of information on Jango Fett's past, seeking to learn whether the man was worthy of being the [[Clone template/Legends|prime clone]] of the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]] being [[Cloning/Legends|cloned]] on [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]].<ref name="OS" /> Fett was ultimately chosen, and as part of the group responsible for training the army, Fett recruited [[Cort Davin]], an ex-[[Journeyman Protector/Legends|Journeyman Protector]] from Concord Dawn. Davin's training of [[Clone Commander/Legends|clone commander]] [[Bacara/Legends|CC-1138]], known as Bacara, led the clone to associate with the traditions of the Protectors and learn the Concord Dawn dialect of [[Mando'a/Legends|Mando'a]]. Others drawn in by the idea of the Protectors and Concord Dawn included [[Fox (501st Legion)/Legends|CT-0000/1010]], or Fox, who sought to become a Protector at the conclusion of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].<ref name="GGAR" /> Another trainer of the Grand Army, [[Kal Skirata]], originally intended to travel to Concord Dawn after the war to locate relatives of the Fetts.<ref name="O66">''[[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel]]''</ref>

In [[16 BBY/Legends|16 BBY]], Jango's son [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] married [[Sintas Vel]] and settled on Concord Dawn under the name of Jaster Mereel, taking up the position of Journeyman Protector and raising a daughter, [[Ailyn Vel|Ailyn]].<ref name="Bloodlines">''[[Legacy of the Force: Bloodlines]]''</ref><ref name="LOS">{{StoryCite|story=The Last One Standing: The Tale of Boba Fett|book=Tales of the Bounty Hunters}}</ref> When Fett's superior officer in the Journeyman Protectors, [[Lenovar]], raped Sintas, Fett killed the man for betraying his uniform.<ref name="Revelation">''[[Legacy of the Force: Revelation]]''</ref> Fett was imprisoned and granted the services of the famous [[Pleader]] [[Iving Creel]] to represent his case. He was unrepentant of the murder, though, and was exiled from Concord Dawn as a result.<ref name="LOS" />

In [[24 ABY/Legends|24 ABY]], a [[Devaronian/Legends|Devaronian]] [[Unidentified Devaronian magistrate|senior magistrate]] on Concord Dawn sympathized with the anti-[[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Diversity Alliance]] movement and relocated certain Human prisoners to the Alliance's headquarters on [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]] to be executed.<ref name="YJK" />

==Inhabitants==
[[File:Fetthomestead.jpg|thumb|right|250px|A farmer's homestead on Concord Dawn.]]
The people of Concord Dawn had close ties to the Mandalorians; a large percentage of Mandalorian genomes had genetic markers indicative of Concord Dawn heritage.<ref name="Mandalorians">{{InsiderCite|86|The Mandalorians: People and Culture}}</ref> However, the natives of Concord Dawn never settled [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]].<ref name="CSWE">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> Instead, the people of Concord Dawn were attracted to Mandalorian culture by shared values, such as a strong sense of self-identity and focus on discipline and physical condition.<ref name="TZ">''[[Republic Commando: Triple Zero]]''</ref> Factors that created a strong sense of loyalty were present in the typical Concord Dawn genome, which the cloners of Kamino used to their advantage by amplifying those traits in Fett's clones.<ref name="O66" /> Mando'a was spoken on Concord Dawn, but its own special [[Concordian/Legends|dialect]]; among the changes were use of the word ''tat'' instead of ''vod'' for "brother".<ref name="GGAR" /> The northern region of the planet had a distinctive accent of [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]] as well.<ref name="Sacrifice">''[[Legacy of the Force: Sacrifice]]''</ref>

Order and peace on Concord Dawn were maintained by the Journeyman Protectors.<ref name="CSWE" /> Cases were given to a Pleader, who would give a plea for his client before a sentence&mdash;anything up to exile or execution&mdash;was decided.<ref name="LOS" /> The law could be strict; cheating at [[Sabacc/Legends|sabacc]], for example, was a capital offense. Laws were heavily enforced on Concord Dawn.<ref name="YJK" />

Notable natives of Concord Dawn included Jaster Mereel, Mandalore of the Mandalorians; Jango Fett, Mandalore and prime clone of the Grand Army of the Republic;<ref name="HOTM" /> [[Cort Davin]], Journeyman Protector and [[Cuy'val Dar]] trainer of the Grand Army;<ref name="GGAR" /> and [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]] [[Sheckil/Legends|Sheckil]], a former warrant officer on the world.<ref name="CCG">{{CCG|set=Cloud City Limited|cardname=Lieutenant Sheckil}}</ref> All inhabitants of Concord Dawn were vaccinated at birth against [[Karatos Plague]], a virus native to the world.<ref name="OS" />

==Behind the scenes==
Concord Dawn originated in [[Daniel Keys Moran]]'s [[1996]] short story "[[The Last One Standing: The Tale of Boba Fett]]", in which it is given as the homeworld of Boba Fett, whose original name is Jaster Mereel.<ref name="LOS" /> ''[[Star Wars: Jango Fett: Open Seasons|Jango Fett: Open Seasons]]'' [[Retroactive continuity|retconned]] this, making Jaster Mereel a separate character and Concord Dawn ''his'' homeworld.<ref name="OS" /> The planet's name bears similarities to [[Battle of Condawn|Condawn]], a location mentioned in the third draft of the original [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'']] film.

''Jango Fett: Open Seasons'' explicitly placed Concord Dawn in the Outer Rim Territories; later works gave it an association with Mandalorian space, also located in the Outer Rim. However, a map released by [[Dark Horse Comics]] at the [[2006]] [[Wikipedia:Comic-Con International|Comic-Con]] placed it in the Mid Rim, far from the planet Mandalore.<ref name="Map">{{DarkHorse|url=Features/Desktops/547/Star-Wars-Galaxy-Map|text=Star Wars Galaxy Map}}</ref> This was one of the errors [[Daniel Wallace|Dan Wallace]] and [[Jason Fry]] corrected in ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', moving Concord Dawn back into Mandalorian space and the Outer Rim.<ref name="Blog">{{Blog|danwallace|144|Endnotes for Star Wars: The Essential Atlas (part 2 of 5)}}</ref>

A diary by the designers of the game ''[[Star Wars: Republic Commando]]'', written in an in-universe style, states that Jango Fett's accent&mdash;actor [[Temuera Morrison]]'s own New Zealand accent&mdash;is a "Concord Dawn inflection," and mentions that some clones adopted it.<ref name="Diary">{{GameSpot|url=articles/star-wars-republic-commando-designer-diary-2-clone-differentiation/1100-6116079|text=Star Wars Republic Commando Designer Diary #2 - Clone Differentiation}}</ref> The novel ''[[Legacy of the Force: Sacrifice]]'' later [[canon]]ically mentioned the existence of a "northern Concordian accent," but does not clarify what it sounds like.<ref name="Sacrifice" />

A [[Wikipedia:New Zealand|New Zealand]] band has since taken the name [[Wikipedia:Concord Dawn|Concord Dawn]].
